transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Well, what brings me in is... I've been having this issue at night. Once I start eating, it feels like I can actually see myself doing it, and I'm telling myself in my head to stop, but... my hands just keep going back for more. I just can't seem to stop once I get going.
During these nighttime eating episodes, would you say you're fully awake and alert, or does it feel more like you're in a groggy, half-asleep state?

I'm... no, I'm definitely awake. I'm not sleepwalking or groggy at all. I'm fully aware of what's happening. Like I said, my mind is completely alert and I'm actively telling myself to stop... I just can't seem to make my hands listen to me.
Does this eating typically happen after you've woken up from sleep in the middle of the night, or is it happening in the evening before you actually go to sleep?
It's before I go to sleep. I don't wake up in the middle of the night to do it. It usually just happens in the evening, you know, before I actually get into bed for the night.
On the mornings after these evening eating episodes, do you typically have little to no appetite or feel like you can't eat breakfast?

No, I wouldn't say that. I... I usually still eat breakfast just fine. I haven't really noticed having no appetite in the mornings after it happens. It just feels like a normal morning for me, appetite-wise.
How often do these evening eating episodes happen each week, and how long have you been experiencing this pattern?

Well, it's been going on for the last several months now. And as for how often... I'd say most weeks there's at least one night where I end up eating like that. Then the whole next day is just... me trying to make up for it. I'll skip meals, or give myself these really strict rules about what I'm allowed to eat, or I'll go for an extra-long walk to try and burn it off.
During these evening eating episodes, would you say you're eating an unusually large amount of food compared to what most people would eat in that same amount of time?

Yeah, I definitely would. I mean... some evenings I'll start with just some leftovers. But then I end up making sandwiches, eating cereal, cookies, and just... whatever snack food is sitting in the pantry. It's far more than I would ever put on a plate for a normal supper, so yeah, it's a lot of food all at once.
When you skip meals or set strict food rules the next day, is that mainly because you're worried about gaining weight or how your body looks, or is it for some other reason?

Yeah, it's... it's definitely about my weight and how I look. It's strange, really. I used to judge my day by whether I solved a tough design problem at work, or maybe how much I helped out at the local theater group I volunteer with. But lately... lately I just look at my stomach in the mirror. It feels like the whole measure of who I am right now is whether I look controlled or... or just sloppy. So yeah, the rules and the skipping meals, it's all because I'm terrified of gaining weight.
